$comment: Shared table for XML 1.0 Char handling. Go's encoding/xml substitutes U+FFFD for every character the Char production forbids and that behaviour is not configurable, so it is the reference; the TypeScript builder must match it because the two are held to byte equality. Each case gives the raw value a converter might carry and the text that must reach the document. Read by both languages: the Go side asserts what encoding/xml actually does, so the expectation is anchored to a real strict encoder rather than to a predicate the emitter and its test both copied.

cases.name: escape sequence in a result message
cases.why: ANSI colour in an InSpec codeDesc — the everyday case, and the one that shipped invalid documents

cases.name: null
cases.why: C0 controls other than tab, LF and CR are outside Char

cases.name: form feed
cases.why: legal in neither XML 1.0 nor either language's whitespace class

cases.name: vertical tab
cases.why: the other C0 character a serializer is likely to meet

cases.name: U+FFFE
cases.why: illegal but not a control character, so a C0-only guard misses it

cases.name: U+FFFF
cases.why: the other non-character at the end of the BMP

cases.name: tab is legal
cases.why: Char admits tab, LF and CR; substituting them would corrupt real text

cases.name: the replacement character itself is legal
cases.why: U+FFFD is inside Char, so a document already carrying one passes through unchanged

cases.name: astral characters are legal
cases.why: above the BMP, where a naive code-unit loop would split a surrogate pair
